Well, madam, folks called me the Borax Kid. My friend, the other rock Alien, died without settin' your genitals to right, so I reckon it's up to me to sex you up proper.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: My girls are back!
The human will be returned to the past!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I love rocket skating! But the wait is always so long. Poor Fry once stood in line for six hours just to get me a ticket.
That's fine too.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It's no use. The tar is too thick. Plus, I think I flooded it.
Only after bringing Project Satan to life did they discover they had made a horrible mistake. For, you see, it was pure evil.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So what happened to Project Satan?
Apology accepted. After all, you're only human.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You guys could learn a lesson from those two.
...still in the abandoned automotive lab.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You guys distract the were-car and I'll kill it by plugging its exhaust pipe with this silver potato.
Well I aim to prove him wrong. It'll take more than a few deadly, deadly bees to-- OH, LORD!!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Uh, couldn't make that out. Too much static.
Aw, man.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Hey, Bender, I thought you said you were in this episode.
What? Seriously? I'm trying to impress you with my clout here.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I know, and it's working. But think how much skating would mean to those kids.
Six hours? Pft! Sounds like a real nobody! But now it's time for somebody and some chick he's with to go skating.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You reserved the whole rink?
Gee, you think? You think that maybe I should use these clamps that I use every day at every opportunity? You're a freaking genius, you idiot!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: The engine's stalled. I'm trying the manual fuel pump.
Approved for demolition.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It's you and me, ponytail.
How do you like me now?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: The toaster's not working right either.
Uh-huh.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Alright. Now there's no way to stop this marriage without hurting Calculon. But he's an actor. If there's one kind of pain he can handle, it's soap opera pain.
Oh, yeah, baby! C'mon! Work your cans! That's it! Shake it out!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I don't know which I'm more Enraged or disgusted.
Certainly not. But just once I'd like to eat dinner with a celebrity who isn't bound and gagged. Is that so much to ask?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well I think you dating a Manbot is a disgrace and I refuse to be involved. And you have way too much lipstick on.
Just doing my job, ma'am.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, Mom, Dad, I can't believe I have to spend the rest of my life in this hellhole. I'm sorry.
At least I still have my self respect!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Who buys this trash?
You suck!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We're hoping to save the animals of Vergon 6 from extinction. And if you could just--
Hey, Leela, help me apply these flame decals I got in my cereal. They'll make the ship go faster.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: And what's your scientific basis for thinking that?
Fry's not here. Obviously he went to that pervert party with Bender and the professor.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Fry went to the party?
What's happening?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: He's hooked up to a life-support system. We have to disconnect him very, very carefully, or the shock could kill him.
Hey!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: If you were my kids, you'd get quite a talking to... from your father... when he got home from the Senate.
My God, the illusion is so perfect I almost forgot I was looking at an idiot!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Now, they may ask for a DNA sample.
Wait a second. That means I also take after you!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Quiet. I think I know how to find the Professor.
Do you think perhaps you and I--

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Fry, you idiot. Ever since I was abandoned on Earth I've been searching for who my people are and where they come from. Then I finally meet another Cyclops and you blast him. You wrecked my one chance to learn who I am!
I saw you in the chat room but you left before I had a chance to talk to you. After all these years of searching for another Cyclops.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I can't believe it. I've dreamed of this moment all my life.
Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, actually, I did mean to offend a little. This is awful.
Don't thank random chance. Thank my meteor-wishing power, with your lips.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Good ending. Not great.
Aren't they? I got them at Nine West.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Simmer down, warriors. Full power to the vagyroscope!
Your eye just needs some rest. You'll have to wear this patch for about a week.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: A week? What do you think, Dr. Zoidberg?
OK. What does this look like to you?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Um... a grey-ish blob?
Right. And this one?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Um... a grey-ish blob?
Proceed.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: These charges are outrageous. Our only goal was to save a rare violet star and its precious ecosystem. If protecting the environment is a crime, then...
You told them about that?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I should've told the truth right away. These simply prairie folk have a simple prairie-ish life here. And I was wrong to exploit it for profit.
Hello, we're the Robot Mafia. The entire Robot Mafia. We're here to steal your cigars.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You'll never get away with this.
Excuse me, I'd like to talk to you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Am I under arrest?
Not anymore. Now I'm the sleazebag who owns the New New York Mets.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: The Mets? Those bums are worse than me.
Close to it. But they don't draw a crowd like you. Which is why I wanna sign you to the team.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You mean I'd be the first woman ever to play Major League Blernsball?
Oh? Then I suppose you also don't believe in... El Chupanibre.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: El Chupanibre? What's that?
Shh. El Chupanibre comes soon. It is nightfall.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Nightfall? How can you tell down here?
Perhaps. But perhaps your civilisation is merely the sewer of an even greater society above you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, we're on the top.
Whatever.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wait. Our pet Nibbler loves fresh crocodile. It's his favourite treat. He must be El Chupanibre.
Yeah, awesome!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Hello, Awesome Express; the rude, crude delivery dudes. How may I direct your call? What's that? You haven't gotten your paper? In how long?
Everybody enjoy their dinner?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Are you kidding me?
What a day for a birthday

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I really would like you to stop singing.
What day is today? Hey, aren't you the loser who got stood up on my other restaurant?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Just shut up and bring me two dinners.
I really appreciate that, mister mayor's aide. Here you go. Compliments of the house.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wow! Free bread at a restaurant? Is there anything you can't do?

Life! These once extinct plants and animals are my gift to the universe. Through untold generations, my race has treasured their DNA. Treat them wisely with the knowledge that all species are precious.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This is unbelievable. What's going on?
The saucers! Theys'a crashin'!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I can't believe TiVo suggested that piece of... Ow! Come on, Hermes. Surely you have the authority to remove this damn collar.

Yes, she's a wonderful ship, all right. As beautiful now as the day I got botched laser eye surgery. Now, that's odd. What's the fuel gauge doing on the fl... Great Godzilla's gonads! Who wasted precious fuel? Answer now or be punished.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: All right, fine. I admit it.
Why is your number seven-eighth's?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: All the whole numbers have been retired.
That was a disgusting story.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: And it's all thanks to Bender. I love you, Bender.
Happy birthday, young Nibbler.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Aww, look how cuddly he looks in his new cape!
Nonsense. It's just like in the song I wrote We all need a new angle on life, You gotta bend away all your trouble and your strife,

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Bender, you've gotta help us.
No. According to this gizmometer, Fry is dead and nothing can bring him back. Remarkable!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: But... my dream. Your science can't unprove that! How could I have known the gift was in Fry's locker?
That's not Fry's jacket. Fry's jacket is red. That's your jacket. An off-the-rack, lime green affair.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: But Fry-- His jacket-- And when I woke up it was on me.
Well, you should've talked louder. Fortunately, I came up with a brilliant idea to save Planet Express. We'll turn it into a commercial airline!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: But that was my idea!
Wait! If we could build an object the exact size, density and consistency of the garbage ball, it might just knock the ball away without smashing it to bits.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: But where can we find a substance the exact density and consistency as garbage?
I'm too young to die!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Come on, before it's too late!

Oh, my, yes. But not this year, because my latest invention is unbeatable. Behold! The death clock. Simply jam your finger in the hole and this read-out tells you exactly how long you have left to live.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Does it really work?
What?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Dwight and Cubert made us a better offer. We're paperboys now.

Ooh, good, Leela. You're here. I'd like to describe my foot pain. My left has a sharp jabbing throb near the bunion, while the other's got a searing pain like gout. Maybe it's too much albumin because of gravity...

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Even if I had a pen, I couldn't write under these conditions. I'm going to some other planet, where I can concentrate.
I don't blame you. Having to wear a costume made from a hollowed-out walrus...

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Everyone, I have a confession. I, Turanga Leela, winner of a Young People's Choice Award, a Peabody Jr, and two Training Emmys, am not what I appear to be. There's something I need to show you.
Baseball?? God forbid!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Face it Fry. Baseball was as boring as mum and apple pie. That's why they jazzed it up.
Shut up!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: For Heaven's Gate, Professor. This ship can do 99% light speed. Why are we going 35 miles an hour?
You see, Og? Everything's running smoothly, yes. And with Fry fired, I can finally leave my jigsaw puzzles out without him eating the pieces.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Forget about Fry. You can hire us back and he'd never have to know.
You're going to do his laundry?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Fry, this is for you.
So that's the situation. Due to the short-sightedness of Old New York, New New York is going to be destroyed by a giant ball of garbage.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Fry, what the hell were you people thinking back then? How could you just throw your garbage away?
I invented it, didn't I? You wouldn't ask Thomas Edison whether he knew how to use a sexmatron.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Halt! What are you doing in this parallelogram of space?
I don't understand. Are you winking or blinking?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Hang on a second.
And the microwave radiation, combined with the gravitons and graviolis from the supernova, blasted us through time itself.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Have you seen today's news?
Help! I'm still in mid-peril, you clods!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: He's too far out! We can't reach him!
Eh, let me just insert lens in microscope. There! Now, for the first time, we may be able to see the infinitesimal fabric of matter itself. Laying bare the most fundamental laws of the universe!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Hey, Fry. I know something you could lay bare.
Or a big fat placebo. It's all the same crap.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Hey, what's rattling around in there?
Hang on. Let me just adjust it to your eye level.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Holy matrimony! That's one flashy rock!
Good work, everyone.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Honestly, that went better than I expected.
Good news, everyone! I've invented a way to turn Bender into a human using a process I call "reverse fossilisation".

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: How does it work?
No fair! You changed the outcome by measuring it.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: How'd you do, Fry?
That is stupid!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I can't believe you're laughing at the tragic exploitation of a proud, bead-loving people.
Can anyone drive stick?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I can. As long as I don't have to parallel park.
What the hell are you talking about?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I don't know. But I'm not helping.
Huh-woh?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I know we're ladies-in-waiting but what are we waiting for?
Leela, have you seen the keys to the spaceship?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I must've left them onboard.
A common— A common cold?! No! No! Ever since Fry first came to us, I've lived in mortal terror that this would happen!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I never heard you mention that.
What?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I said we'll go to the jungle and let Guenter decide once and for all.
What say you, Single Female Lawyer?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I say... I'm giving up the law. And I'm giving up being single. Your Honour, will you marry me?
Jungles? On Earth?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I see some movement up there. I think it's him.
I'm your man.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I vote my 10,000 shares for the Professor.
I had a few beers but I'm cool to drive.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I wish I could come with you to say goodbye, before you all turn back in to grown-ups but I'm grounded for knocking the school over.
What do you mean "no power"? We're living in the future.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I'd better light some candles.
It's working! Hooray! I can't hold on!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I'm coming in after you!

Shut up, Hawking. Fry, you idiot! You're a genius! Why are the laws of physics what they are? Instead of some other laws? To find out, we'd have to recreate the conditions before the Big Bang. It would take decades of work by thousands of scientists in a particle accelerator powered by dump trucks of flaming grant money. Of course, there'd be no guarantee of success. And, in any case, I'd never live to see it.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I'm surprised you lived through that sentence.
Oh, dear. Her mood swings are getting wilder. She's becoming a slave to her emotions. Just like all women. Particularly you, Leela.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I'm worried about him too, Professor.

Here we go. Just unhook it and get the remote. So many hooks! Come on, Farnsworth. Drat, the first one's back on again! I give up! Wait! Victory! Oh, my. Now I'll just... the remote... I'll just... Oh, my!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I'm worried. It shouldn't take this long to get to second base.
Get out there!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Is everybody in position?
Lay down here and we'll do some tests. If Fry is out there then Leela's brain could be acting as a five-pound Ouija board.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Is this some sort of brain scanner?
So? Lots of important inventions are made from toilet paper tubes. Microscopes, the internet, tentacle polish...

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It got the professor!
It was as though I were living in a facility in Florida with hundreds of other old people. All day long we'd play bingo, eat oatmeal and wait for our children to call.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It's a hundred times more horrible than anything I could imagine.
Good news! We're back in business. We've been hired to deliver an envelope.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It's crunch time. Let's do this. It's for you, Professor.
That's not what happened! Shut up and go live with your parents.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It's gonna be totally awesome, Mom! You and me can bake and argue about my hairstyle hiding my pretty face. And if some kid picks on me, my dad can beat up his dad.
Huh? You were gone?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It's just that I get tired of Fry always only thinking of himself.
Yes. The science mobile!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It's just that you've never called it that before, but okay.

Things only rhyme below ten to the minus five angstroms, you dope! Now, ions an' pions, muons an' gluons, neutrinos, gravitinos... We're closing in on the very smallest particles of matter! For the first time, we're about to observe the fundamental structure of the universe. Such detail. Such finely wrought intricate beauty!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It's like staring into the face of God!
Five, four, three, two, three, four, five, six...

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Just fire the damn thing.
They robbed me of my dignity And most of my stuff.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Lars brought me candy.
Ah! The desert muck leech. Amazingly, the entire species lives in this one tiny stink hole. Killing these will be so much easier than exterminating those ponies.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Leeches may not be cuddly like pandas or tribbles, but these poor endangered creatures deserve... Get off me!
I've warned you not to use those things!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Let's see. We've got our malt, our hops. We just need a big disposable tub to mix it in.
And I hit Farnsworth much, much harder. Eh, perhaps too hard.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Look! All the Presidents are back! Even John Tyler!
Help! Satan! You owe me!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Look, um, I'm embarrassed to admit this but you forced me to I can't go out tonight because... I have sweaty boot rash.
What's all the hubbub?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: My God! Even the Professor's been bent.
What is happening?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Nibbler, you... You can talk?
Yes, we tore the universe a new space-hole alright! But it's clenching shut fast. Our only hope to get back to our own time is to go through it in, oh, say... exactly 24 hours.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No problem. The ship's fixed except for the cup holder and I should have that operational within 10 hours.
And you, Coach Smalley, or should I say "Coach hairpiece"?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, Professor! It's a surprise party for your 150th birthday.
What I love most about the tentacle is that I don't need to move my bowels anymore. It's all handled by that family in Evanston.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, it can't be.
My life is over.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, it isn't. You have another 10 years left.
Now, it's not hard to spot a phoney Internet come-on. "Get rich quick x7 q"? Phoney. "Lose weight with space parasites"? Phoney. What's this? I've won the Spanish National Lottery?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, it's a scam!
Oh, fiddlepoop! Our weapons aren't strong enough to puncture a thin plastic tent that thick?!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No. But theirs are!
Horray denied! Need I remind you that robosexual marriage is illegal!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Not in Space Massachusetts.
It used to be that every group in New New York wanted their own parade. Why, when I was a boy, we had a parade every day. Those were dark times.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Now we just combine them all into one big Parade Day parade and get it over with.
But I like being old. I don't have to talk to my parents, no one asks me to help move their stuff, I don't need to understand today's "edgy" TV sitcoms.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: OK, OK. We're not gonna force you until I finish this sentence. Get him!
I just told you, you've killed me!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: OK, just try to be nonchalant.
You're falling into the final debilitating stages of womanhood. You've waited too long to switch back, you ding bat!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: OK, look. If I help you with this do you promise to get out of my gender and stay out?
Would you all chill! I can't think with you kids cramping my style! Oh, I need a babysitter.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: OK, quiet time. I know, everyone pretend a goblin ate your tongue and I'll read you a story.
Now, now, there'll be plenty of time to discuss your objections when and if you return.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Odour at magnitude 8. Magnitude 12. Magnitude 31. We're breaking up. Turn on the anti-smell device.
Ooh! Oh, you've killed me! You've killed me!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, God! What have I done?
Good heavens! Trilobots!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, no! My sunglasses were in there!
That is what you're looking at.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh. How could you do this, Fry?
Oh, call me an old fool, but I believe the Lord is speaking through you. Brace yourselves, everyone!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: One hundred kilometers! Two hundred!
I'm glad you're so brave in the face of the unknown, Leela. Because, for your next mission, you'll be flying directly through... The Bermuda Tetrahedron!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Or we could fly around it.
Because we're in a hurry, that's why.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Plus, you have the high beams on!
Some sort, yes. In France it's called a guillotine.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Professor! Can't you examine my brain without removing it?
It will if we go back in time and stop him!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Professor, no! You can't tongue the father of our country!
Cygnoids? On our block? Flying foo! They should go back where they came from.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Professor, please! Society's never gonna make any progress until we all learn to pretend to like each other. Now let's go over there and make these hideous strangers feel welcome.
Oh! I'm blind!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Professor, we have no power.
Mmm! Damn good meat!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Professor, we've talked it over and everybody thinks you're too old.
Greedy old hag, taste the wrath of my fuzzy slipper.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Professor, why are you so hot and dusty over this dark matter shortage?
Eh, wha? I mean, what?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Relax. The ship's not going anywhere. I anchored it with the unbreakable diamond tether.
Oh, poor Guenter.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So he just ran away in the middle of the exam?
Ahhh, that soothes the fire.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So what does this mean for us and our many fans?
Cute as a baby's buttocks.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So what happened? How did Mom capture all you Nibblonians?
There. That space-time eversion has given us their box and vice versa.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So, what you think you just explained to us is that--
Leela, you ignorant dope! Now the worms will be in Fry forever.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So? Did you ever stop to think that Fry is better off with worms?
The main pit must be in here. I'm detecting vast quantities of Dark Matter.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Step aside turkey-neck. I think I know the code.
Indeed so. This whole area will be incinerated when he implodes that sun there into a black hole.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That beautiful violet star?
Pandora.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That dangerous, 3-D planet? Can't we just send our avatars?
Collecting honey. Ordinary honey.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That doesn't sound so dangerous.
Yes, but something he saw on that mission traumatised 'im so severely, he grew hair! Just so it could turn white! Sadly, my brave crew was gone forever.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That poor, incompetent crew. What do you think happened, Professor?
Poor, ignorant Leela. The bone vampire is now extinct on its home planet.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's perfect! We can reintroduce it to the wild and repopulate the species!
There. I've finished fine-tuning my What-If machine. It can answer any "What-If" question, accurate to within one-tenth of a plausibility unit.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's so plausible I can't believe it!
Cha-ching!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: The teleporter gun? But that means Fry might still be...
You can't just waltz into the Central Bureaucracy. It's a tangled web of red tape and regulations. I've never been but a friend of mine went completely mad trying to find the washroom there.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Then we'll need a guide. Someone who's been there before.
I wish I exuded anything that smelled half that good.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Then what about these angels? Some kind of Scooby Doo-esque flashlight projection?
Then you should've talked louder. What?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: There. It was hard work, but it beats posing in demeaning, skimpy modelling outfits.
Well, in those days Mars was just a dreary, uninhabitable wasteland, uh, much like Utah. But unlike Utah, it was eventually made livable, when the university was founded in 2636.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: They planted traditional college foliage; ivy, trees, hemp. Soon the whole planet was terraformed.
They pooh-poohed my electric frankfurter.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: They said I probably shouldn't fly with just one eye.
Go ahead, get into these net suits. I designed and tested them myself.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: They smell like burning Rhesus Monkey.
Ah, here they come.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: They're in attack formation. They're going to kill us! That was weird. It's like the Jägermeister air show all over again.
Behold My mutant atomic supermen.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: They're only a foot high, Professor.
We could but we won't! It's a spaceship, damnit, not a prom limousine! If anyone needs me I'll be in the Angry Dome.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This is a very long trip. So we'll all have to go into hibernative-naptosis to save oxygen.
Deciphering that ID code is critical. I'll be in the Chamber of Understanding.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This is it! The moment we should've trained for!
This is an outrage! I demand you hand over your captain's jacket.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This is my normal jacket. I've had it for 10 years.
No, not me. I'm too busy developing makeup for dogs. That's where the money is.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This is our chance to teach Mom a lesson. Let's take the anti-crystal and shove it up Mom's regular crystal.
My god! It's the Pantheon!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This place is 3,000 years old. What could possibly be left to discover?
What are you yapping about?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This time it's your reckless disregard for the environment. In fact, I'm gonna go join those protestors.
Nonsense. Now click your big, honking boots together three times and wish to go home to Kansas, to live in poverty with your dirt-farming, teetotalling aunt and uncle.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Uh, alright. Here I go. There's no place like-- I wanna be a witch! Oh, no! Help! What's happening?
Let's get this gargoyle hunt on the road. Driving gloves, driving goggles, driving thong. There!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Uh, maybe I should drive.
Oh, Lord! We'll have to endure the horrible music of the Big Bopper and then the terrible tragedy of his death.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wait a second! There's a microwave radar dish at the army base. We could steal it!
Ouch! That's going to bleed when my heart beats.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wait! Take me first!
That's right. Animals in desperate need of rescue. You see, Vergon 6 was once filled with a super-dense substance known as dark matter, each pound of which weighs over ten thousand pounds.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wait! What about the animals?
Wha?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wait. If you killed your grandfather, why do you still exist?

Oh, how awful. Did he at least die painlessly? To shreds, you say. Well, how is his wife holding up? To shreds, you say. Very well then. Sad, sad, terrible, gruesome news about my colleague, Dr. Mbutu.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Was his apartment rent-controlled?
Aw. I suppose there's nothing left to do but move out. Leela, Amy, pack us a lunch for our new lives under the bridge while us men reminisce and smoke some stogies.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We are not packing lunches, you walking beer commercials. It was you men who drove this company into the ground. Remember Fry's idea to offer free delivery?
Fry, you dope! You've really screwed the granny this time! History needed that second lantern!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We better stop Paul Revere before—
Oh, dear! I really ought to do something. But I am already in my pyjamas.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We can't outrun it forever.
Cover that fireplace, confound you! I've only a few years to live. I don't wanna spend them dead.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We're pushing as hard as we can.
Shut up! I was gonna say that!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We've got to hurry. The kids have only one change of pants!
Let's go, already. We've got to infiltrate Mom's dark matter mine, now. How do you start this thing? Good Lord, woman. Can you move any slower? Rake up some dark matter and top off the tank.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, there isn't any dark matter. Nibbler hasn't pooped at all. And he ate a whole family of koalas last night. Nibbler! Nibbler!
Thanks for the help, Weewa. Once we're gwown up, you can go back to your famiwy. We'wl never bother you again.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, you could bother me a little.
Tonight is the ribbon-cutting for the DOOP's new headquarters.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What are we delivering?
You've gone too far this time -- all three of you!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What did I do?
I can, but that's because I'm not a penniless hippie.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What do you people want?
Good news, everyone! The university is bringing me up on disciplinary charges. Wait, that's not good news at all.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Whatever you did, Professor, I'm sure there's a reasonable explanation.
Certainly not. Two dings means it's done. But not like that. Slightly more rapid.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Where did they go?
Correct. 6,000 hulls.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Why do we have to fly within three feet of this penguin preserve on Pluto?
Good news, everyone! We were supposed to make a delivery to the planet Tweenis 12 but it's been completely destroyed.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Why is that good news?
Faster! Faster! Just drop me off at that asteroid over there.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wow, this planetoid is completely lifeless.
No harm done. In the many decades you'll work to repay me for that shipment of popcorn you destroyed, you'll have plenty of time to search for your true home.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yeah. I mean, how many planets can there be?
Well, dark matter is extremely valuable as starship fuel. That's why it was all mined out, leaving the planet completely hollow.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yes, but what about the animals?
You'll be picking up a monument commemorating my lost crew. To be unveiled Tuesday at their memorial ceremony. All the grieving families will be there. Plus, a popsicle cart!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You can count on us, Professor. We'll get that monument here in time.
Evolution is under attack in our schools? To the science mobile.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You mean the ship?
Uh... Jenny McNeal, you are charged with jury-tampering in last week's case... on account of your hot, naked affair with the foreman. How do you plead?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Your Honour, I move for a mistrial, on the grounds that I'm also having a hot, naked affair with the foreman of this jury.
That a girl! If they don't take him back we can keep him as captain.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Your Honour, it's all true My female incompetence, Zapp's cat-like reflexes, the stuff that made no sense, all of it.
Everybody out of the conference room. I am calling a conference. Everybody get in here. You wasted precious fuel just because you were insulted by some redneck yokel from beyond the stars?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It was only half a ball.
Emergency! Emergency! Everyone to the Calamitorium! Leela, smell this.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Can I wipe it off first?
We're perfectly safe now. Time to stop living like a bunch of nervous nellies.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Professor, these look like you cut them from cardboard toilet paper tubes.

dialogue.text: Where is the great fountain?

dialogue.text: This will make a great episode. But talk slower. I can't type that fast.
All medallists report for gender testing.

This is Turanga Leela's first nomination and second time in high heels.

dialogue.text: Wow. I feel so lucky just to have been nominated alongside so many inferior shows. And, to all my young friends at the Orphanarium, thank you for inspiring me to be your hero.
Uh, good. Good.

dialogue.text: So, your real name is Lord Nibbler? That's a coincidence.
Only Fry, with his superior, yet inferior mind, can approach him. You must tell him to disable it. We will do the rest.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You can count on me.
No shoot him, he's choking me!

dialogue.text: I don't know which one to shoot.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I lost my chance to be a champion. I won't let you throw away yours.
So, we meet again. Most amusing Girl who acts like fighter training fighter who acts like girl.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Keep laughing, Fnog! Ready, Bender?
I am Destructor's trainer, Master Fnog. My pupil will be victorious for he has the will of a warrior!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Not Fnog! Bender, let's hit the gym. I'm gonna teach you to fight like a girl!
No girl has the will of a warrior. You have the will of a housewife or, at best, the schoolmarm.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's it. I'll take you on right now.
Perhaps. But there is more to winning than beating your opponent. You lack the will of the warrior.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What do you mean? Watch this!
Huh?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You didn't train Destructor. You're just controlling him like a puppet. I mean, cheating in a fake fight. That's low!
It's not-not a smart bet.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: According to the script, you're supposed to prance out and tickle him with your fairy wand. Instead, I want you to prance out and kick his head off!
Yes! Front row!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You can't go to Omega 3; it's forbidden! I forbid you!
My two favourite things are commitment and changing myself.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Does that dummy have a brother?
Could we still use our bullhorns?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Absolutely. Bullhorns are a core principle of eco-feminism.
Here's the button here. And I think I... Now I got it.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Let me give you a hand.
We are the Greenorita Eco-Feminist Collective, and we will not let you...What was it again?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We will not let you implode the violet dwarf star at galactic coordinates 167.84, -58.03, mark 948.
Then I'm in.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Who's ready to kick some sweaty man-butt?
...well, that's only 'cause she had so much of real Leela in her. I thought she loved me, too, but, obviously, I was wrong as usual.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wrong again. You were right.
I can't take it, Leela. I need to go away. Far away, forever.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Aw, I know how you feel, Fry. There are times when I also feel like you need to go away.
Just wake up, Leela. Please. Just wake up.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I don't understand what you mean!
I don't know if you can hear me, Leela, but there's something I wanna tell you. I love you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I'm so scared, Fry. I don't know what to do.
You can! The Leela I know doesn't give up this easily.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: OK. I'll try. Go away!
Leela! No! Listen to me, you don't want to lie in bed like a vegetable and do nothing the rest of your life. I've tried it. Bedsores hurt!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Then what am I s'posed to do?

There's no one here whose thoughts can't be read. No one, except me! My thoughts can't be read. But, but that's crazy. If I were the Dark One, I'd know it, wouldn't I? But, here I am, right where the Dark One would be, about to blow up the star. Oh, God! Somewhere deep inside of me, it's me! I'm the Dark One!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Put your hands in the air!
I'm a banking industry regulator.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Really? Y'know, I heard that banking industry regulations are really very simple.
Get me the President.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Fry's from around this time. I'll talk like him. Yo, homes! We're looking for a microwave oven.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Dismiss all charges? Your Honour, I know the case is closed and you've rendered your verdict, but I wanna testify.
That's right. They think they have a good union but they don't. They're basically slaves.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What are you doing?
Well, my curious friends, you learned the secret of Slurm. That concludes the portion of the tour where you stay alive.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You wish, you slimy worm! Hi-yah!
Please don't tell my supervisor I was sleeping.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This is it. We'll just run in, grab Bender's disk and run out. Got it?
I can't tell you. What do I look like? A grade 16?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We're getting nowhere slowly. Here, I'll address this to the Central Filing room. Then we'll track it using my wrist LoJack-a-mater.
Ere you go. "In memory of the 1st Planet Express ship and it's crew".

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Hang on. It's shouldn't have an apostrophe. This means and it is crew. What the hell's wrong with you?!
It's a minor error, lady. I mean, we're space Aliens. It's a miracle we can even speak English.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: The miracle is that I'm not kickin' your ass! I insist you recarve the entire statue correctly.
I wuv my Mommy!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So how are you gonna lug all those gifts to Mom's factory?
Hail! Hail! Hail!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So after I specifically asked you not to touch anything, you drank a bottle of strange blue liquid? It could have been poisonous acid!
Leave me alone.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Hey, what's going on? I thought you didn't like bananas.
I'd rather live in a crate than share a room with this dork.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So what makes Guenter talk?
So what? I mean, sure, it looks cool and it makes me smart but it doesn't make me happy.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's so sad. I didn't even know monkeys could cry.
Now go! Go! Uh, could one of you just-- Ah, forget it. I'll just sleep here.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: There. No rampaging for you tonight.
But I'm not done vomiting.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I can't stand it! OK. You can have my hand.
A man writing an opera about a woman? Oh, sirrah, how deliciously absurd! I shall see you at the premiere.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Is it part of the opera?
What shklee's actually doing.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: ...is mating with you! These aren't tentacles. They're genticles.
It's an important unit.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: And this, my friends, is the L-unit I just removed from the ship.
Did you see that?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Are you okay? What just happened?
Easy! He told you about it before he died and your grief-roasted mind blocked it out.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Are you saying I'm going crazy?
I feel dirty.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Are you sure Fry is working for your father? It just doesn't seem like him to be so evil, or to hold down a job.
Sweet honey bee of infinity!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Bender! Quit destroying the universe!
I'm from Jamaica, the "Show Me" island. So show me you're blowing it out your fanny.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: But he gave me his jacket. Look.
Now he's wearing a hat!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Come on, let's all sing Happy Birthday!
You been hittin' the Red Stripe, woman!

dialogue.text: Comport yourself, Mr. Conrad! When we're at space, the Captain's word is law. I could marry you and Bender against your will if I wanted to.
OK, Captain, this is just a standard legal release protecting Planet Express from lawsuits in the event of the unforeseen.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Death by airlock failure.
My Speedos!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Depth at 45 hundred feet, 48 hundred, 50 hundred! 5000 feet!
All opposed? All abstaining?

dialogue.text: Duh. That's why we all came over here for lunch. Send.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Get out of my office!
Oh, this is great!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Glad you could make it.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Hermes, that's sweet. I didn't know you cared about Nibbler.
And now you're asking for a day off? Get out of my and my sight! You're bogarting my patience.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Hermes, who were you yelling at?
Goodbye, Mr. Dumbsworth!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Hey! This my chance to spend time with my parents too.
Yeah. Last time you went to the suicide booth, you ended up dating it for six months.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: How is Lynn, by the way?
Leela.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: How is this possible? And can you believe she wore a tank top to my funeral?
Look at you!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Hubba-hubba. Your pants go almost all the way to your ankles!
You're under a lot of guilt stress, Leela. Here, work it off.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I am not under stress, damnit!
That's my boy!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I guess this is a... Not so bad. As long as we don't need to use our mental... Mental...
I think I'm coming down with circusitis.

dialogue.text: I thought circusitis only affected children.
I don't want you to worry about your jobs while you're away. That's why I'm firing you now.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I wanna enlist. My friends always die if I'm not there to save them.

Finally, the last form of the day. Welcome to Stampy Town. Population, five! And now for the finishing touch. Ah, the cycle of bureaucracy. Sweet gorilla of Manila! A letter from the Central Bureaucracy! Attention, Hermes Conrad You are about to receive a letter from the Central Bureaucracy. My God! It's from the Central Bureaucracy!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I'm having a poker game tonight with some friends from my old cryogenics job. You guys interested?
Ah! Time for my precious 10am meeting. Where in Legoland is Leela?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I'm here and I'm getting along just fine, thank you. My walk to work today just took a little longer than usual. Nibbler took me through the zoo for some reason.
We're saved!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: I've been thinking a lot about moving on with my life. And hearing the words Nibbler on the Roof has given me the kick in the pants I needed. It's time for me to leave and make a fresh start.
Why are you protecting Zoidberg, Professor? Do you owe him something?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Is he blackmailing you somehow?
Faster!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It won't move. And the door release is on the other side.
No, no, no.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It'll take more than deadly, deadly bees to keep us from doing our job. Come on, boys.
Stick to someone else, you windy barnacle!

dialogue.text: It's funny how the battle of the sexes was only resolved when a Manbot and a Fembot realised they loved each other.
He must've gone out looking for that mermaid. The poor, demented honky.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: It's ocean madness alright. Sailors call it aqua dementia, the deep-down crazies, the wet willies, the screaming moist!
He's Barbados Slim And I'm Jamaican fat. Who would choose a backwards corpse With lice in his hair?

dialogue.text: Lars says I'm dreamy.

dialogue.text: Let's see you beat it, Rastaman.

dialogue.text: Look, I agree that it makes space walking more comfortable, but, for a photo shoot, it's a little... Unsavoury. Over.

dialogue.text: Look, I don't know about any of your previous captains but I intend to do as little dying as possible.
Kingston rules. Two men go down, one come up.

dialogue.text: Look, the Professor trusts me with a giant spaceship. He wouldn't trust the rest of you with his dentures.

dialogue.text: Mmm. The ingredients are cooked. And they've picked up some of your natural robot flavourings. Time to add the yeast.

dialogue.text: Nobody panic! Just get to the panic room!

dialogue.text: OK, everyone, calm down. The Professor and I will get to work on the ship. Bender, Zoidberg, since you can survive underwater, you'll go out and look for food.
It's nobody. Now sign that will I gave you! He's not here.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, for the love of Benji!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh. Then I have a new vow. I solemnly swear that I will become not the worst blernsball player of all time.
Look at all these famous lost ships. There's the Garmin. And the TomTom.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Over there! It's the original Planet Express ship!
So... Tell us. How's the intergalactic real estate going?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I just sold a castle to the King of Space. But, somehow, I keep finding myself thinking about this place. An' things.
Sweet squid of Madrid! The tentacle got Fry!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Quick, hand me my machete! We can still save his legs!
Uh... no.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Someone should tell him.

dialogue.text: Sure. Bare hands or weapon?
That's Leela!

dialogue.text: Thank you, Professor. I'm happy that Bender can finally feel my pain.
Perhaps the Professor's files can clear things up. "Citation for public nudity", "Conspiracy to commit public nudity". Aha! A new will! Naming... you as his sole heir.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That doesn't prove I killed him.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's it! I warned you. Fry, Zoidberg, I now pronounce you man and—
Zagtar was destroyed by the crystal space devil!

dialogue.text: Then that's what I am! Hi-yah!
As long as we eat 'er filthy scrambled eggs, you'll never find out.

Was a substantial loss for the company. The blue slice represents the money we earned from shipping packages, while the green slice represents an $8 bank error in our favour.

dialogue.text: This toads the wet sprocket. What about out thousands of shares of stock?

dialogue.text: Too much papers! Not enough hiding plants!
We'll start by slashing salaries, and this time I mean really slashing.

dialogue.text: Uh, guys, I don't know how to tell you this, so I'll just let Fry blurt it out thoughtlessly.
Oh, God, no! Get out of here, you horrific sausage!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wait! Isn't today the parade? It's just a giant balloon!
My Manwich!
