dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Let's see. If that's Hypodermic Ridge then the bomb must go right here. Get ready to run. We've got 25 minutes. Uh, 15 minutes. 5 minutes. "6h" minutes?
Wow! A superpowers drug you can just rub into your skin? You'd think it'd be something you have to freebase.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Let's see. Which powers do we have? Super-strength?
Darth Stroyer? That’s the stupidest name I’ve ever heard.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Let’s hear the rest.
But, Leela, we're no good.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Listen, I'm scared too. But I'm more scared of disappointing myself.
Oh right. I wonder where they all smoke in high school.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Listen. Just go behind those garbage cans. I'll stand guard.
So?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Look at all these guys. Do you have any idea what the average length of their reigns was?
Oh, it's Bender's apartment. He put in carpeting yesterday so now my head hits the ceiling. Hey, do you realise you're standing at a weird angle? Now you're OK.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Look at yourself. You're a wreck! You've got to find a new place to live.
Bees make honey and jelly? Huh. How come nothing humans make tastes good? Help! I can't swim in jelly, as far as I know!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Look! It's a baby queen! Aw, she's so cute! You adorable wittle, itty-bitty, fuzzy-wuzzy--
The corner! Why didn't I think of that?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Look, Fry, I'd like to help you but it's my wedding and I'm kind of busy. Here. Try to be happy for me. That way at least one of us will be.
Oh, can't you leave me alone? I'm miserable enough already.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Look, I know it's not much consolation but I understand how you feel.
Sir, I'm outfitting an expedition to a monastery high in the Himalayas. I'll need a long-sleeved coat.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Look, I miss Bender almost half as much as you do but you can't bring him back this way. It's hopeless.
Is that an invitation?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Love your optimism, Fry. But seriously, you've got to tell Bender you're moving out.
Those Swedes sure know how to put in almost everything you need.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Man, I'm sore all over. I feel like I just went ten rounds with Mighty Thor.
Like this is not the end. But mostly just, I love you, Leela.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Maybe I waited too long to say this, but I love you, too- wormhole!
Definitely. Or... Somewhere else.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Maybe I'm havin' some kinda... Early-life crisis, but... Look Don't you ever wonder about the future?
Yeah but I guess I'd be angry too if I had to go to some uninhabited planet.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Maybe we ought to do something nice for him.
Blech! We have to track down my nose before some alien snarfs it and does the worm. Who's in?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Me and Bender and maybe Zoidberg if he feels like it.
What just happened?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Miller's on a pace to hit 70 blerns!
Surprise!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Mind if we crash here tonight? The colours in the van are keeping us awake.
Leela, I want you to know I think the way you moved those stars around was really wonderful. I got you something.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Moderately-priced, domestic, non-vintage champagne? How did you know?
Well, I guess we'd better clean up these millions of hearts.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Nah, I've got a lazier idea.
Cool! Let's see this one!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Nah. I'm not in the mood for a historical documentary. I've heard good things about Quizblorg, Quizblorg.
It was called... let me think. It was really famous -- Ruth Gordon had one. The wheel!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Never heard of it.
Hey, cool! Dark side of the moon!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Nightfall's coming. Hurry, before we freeze.
Leela's got a boyfriend!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No I don't. But I think we ought to meet with him and see if he'll help us rescue those animals.
Hey! [He yelps as he's constantly swung out of harm's way.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No effect. The crystals are bouncing off the tentacle like meatballs off Mothra.
Man, lucky for us Zapp Brannigan's nearby.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No way! Forget it! I refuse to go crawling back to him!
Oh my God! We have to go down and rescue him.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No we can't! They'll kill us on sight.
Yeah, a barbecue! I'll wear my hilarious apron.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No! I don't care how hilarious your apron is, we're not cooking him. Aww! I'll call him Nibbler.
Leela, we're missing the premiere. My only goal in life was to attend a Hollywood shindig. Just pay the valet the two bucks.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No! It's the principle of the thing. Besides, I think I see a parking lot up ahead.
Ow! It bit my finger!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No! No! It's tasted human blood!
I know but I forgive you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, Fry, by "close quarters" I mean this office--
Cool, an alien! Has your race taken over the Earth?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, I just work here.
Are you still mad at me for wrecking your once-in-a-lifetime chance to learn the meaning of your existence?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, I'm just happy you were able to win a video game. Now let's concentrate on getting this desperately-needed popcorn to the people of Cineplex 14, OK?
Man, it's hot! How hot is it? It's so hot, I poured McDonald's coffee in my lap to cool off. Johnny Carson said it.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, Nibbler! Don't drink the pool water! It's full of chlorine!
He didn't?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, and with wind-chill it's 20 degrees below absolute zero. I'd better go find him.
No. Do you?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, but I used to play the drums. They're sorta similar. What happens if we lose?
Leela! He could live another 100 years!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, he couldn't. When you turn 160, robots from the Sunset Squad take you to a mysterious planet and you never return.
I'm sorry, Leela. I hope that didn't make you ashamed to be seen with me.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, it only makes you more attractive.
You can. All you have to do is wake up.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, no! Don't say that! This is real!
Hey, I plan on having a few brewskis myself.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, they were assassinated. In fact, the law says you'll be killed on the spot if you fail to recite the oath from memory.
Well, what do you suggest? A daring daylight robbery of Fort Knox on elephant-back? That's the dumbest thing I ever heard!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, we can get jobs.
Well, maybe you'll meet someone else someday.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, you don't understand. Lars is the only man I'll ever love. I know it in my heart.
Admit it! You're disgusted by me!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No, you're disgusted by me!
Bend-er? Doesn't ring a bell. Did you hear something, Leela?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No. But I bet it wasn't someone who was good at stealing.
We're gonna die! It's every man for himself! Help me, Leela! You did it! We're safe!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No. Now we're gonna die.
Who does he think he is, being polite to you? You want me to beat him up?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No. Stop being so immature.
My God. What if the secret ingredient... is people?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: No. There's already a soda like that Soylent Cola.
Listen, Leela, let me make it up by taking you out to dinner tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Nope. I've got a date with Chaz.
Uh, Leela, how you gonna meet your folks tomorrow? We've already scheduled the Zookeeper for a 9am foiling at the museum.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Not a problem. I've cleverly arranged to meet my parents right there at the same museum at 10.
Oh, you're not so shallow that you find me repulsive because of my body, are you?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Not at all. Amy, stop it! Fry, help! She's turning me into a parade float!
So Leela's in your body?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Not exactly. Aha! You do only like me for my body.
We're gonna crash!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Not if I can help it! Oh, I guess I can't. Everyone, put on your seatbelts.
This is every bit as fun as the real Civil War.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Not the Civil War private. We’re reinacting the Sith-il War.
What? What are you talking about?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Nothing. We just talked.
Have you seen my sombrero?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Now he's flushed himself down the toilet? Who's he gonna flush next?
Thanks, eagle eye.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Now it's daylight, so he should be in robot form. But be careful Many robots are stupid and violent.
I'm not scared of that at all.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Now, bees communicate by dancing.
Same as everyday, got it.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Now, here's the plan.
So where are we going anyway?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Nowhere special. The moon.
Oh. Kinda like how a warehouse is inhabited by boxes.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: OK Bender, we're here. It's time to get to work.
I burned my finger.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: OK, check the guidebook.
Yes, I am. I simply haven't discovered my primary function yet.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: OK, this has gotta stop. I'm going to remind Fry of his humanity the way only a woman can.
Wait, hold on. I don't like the sound of that. Let's just go alphabetically.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: OK. First Bender, then Flexo, then Fry.
Wait, let's go by rank.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: OK. First Bender, then Flexo, then Fry.
God help us!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: OK. Keep an eyeout for Bender.
Leela! You're alive!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Of course I'm alive.
Leela! You're awake!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Of course I'm awake. You wouldn't stop waking me. Where am I?
Lighten up, Leela. It's funny!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Of course it is. But you don't have to laugh!
Mmm. There's nothin' wrong with a little fast food once or twice a meal. Heart... Attack! I'm fine.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh! I got a bone in my fruit! That's it. From now on, we're not eating anything unless we know what it is an' where it's from. We're going to the local farmers market.
When I'm with you, every day seems like double-soup Tuesday.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, Fry! I love what you've become.
Then what if we shared a sleigh ride across the ice fields of Hyperion?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, Fry! You must be alive; I've never been treated so romantically by my own imagination before.
So's a peacock but you don't eat it until it's cooked. This has to be perfect. I want you to hear exactly what I hear when I think about you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, Fry. All this time you've had this incredible gift and I never knew. I've been a fool. A fully-justified, prudent fool. They're so cold.
It's been two weeks. You wanna play tic-tac-toe again before we eat our shoes?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, I always knew I'd die at the bottom of a pit. But a pit full of tar?
I'm talking about Flexo.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, I get it. This is cute. You're jealous of Bender's new friend!
And also, for some reason, the letter I wrote you full of my personal feelings.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, I'm scared! My whole life has just been a show for some perverted mutant!
Oh, look, I'm not actually interested in her if that's what's bothering you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, are you sure? I mean, she has two eyes, you have two eyes.
I don't know why my brother hated me so much.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, brothers always fight. I'm sure deep down he loved you. He just never got a chance to say it before you got frozen.
Well it's not my fault either 'cause I forgot to vote.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, crud. I knew there was something I meant to do today.
Negative. I must be a robot. Why else would human women refuse to date me?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, lots of reasons.
Preciate it, Guenter!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, no! Hurry, Guenter, climb up the vine. You can still save yourself.
We climbed a mountain and locked up some monks.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, no! The monks! We forgot to let them out of the laundry room.
Hey, Project Satan! Over here! I'm a blind pedestrian! 20 points!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, no! There's no exhaust pipe!

What? No. I told her to tell you that I'm... Oh, Jeep! The Dark Ones got her. It's all true. We need to talk, Leela. Then I can explain... Well, I can't explain anything, but we should talk anyway. Where are you?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, no. I'm not gonna expose the Honeybun Hideout. Where are you?
Sorry, ladies. Employees only.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, no. They're forming a human pyramid... of robots.
Maybe Yivo was right. Maybe I should look for love closer to home. I don't know, Leela, you think maybe...

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, please. You forgot me quick enough when you met Colleen.
That's not how it happened.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, really? I don't see you with a fun-gineering degree!
You guys are crazy. Leela doesn't need surgery. You look great the way you are.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, that's so sweet, Fry. But for once in my life, I just wanna look normal.
I think the view's perfect already!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, that's the corniest thing I've ever heard! Let me show you the bedroom.
Duh. Hey, is it safe to talk while you're flying?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, totally. This thing's hands-free. That's how I can eat this taco and this spaghetti.
Christmas. You know? X-M-A-S.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh, you mean Xmas. You must be using an archaic pronunciation. Like when you say "ask" instead of "aks".
In New York? Bathrooms.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh. I-I'll be out in a sec.
Leela, listen. You're the most beautiful woman I've ever known.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh. So you only care about my looks?
Eww! look at her!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh. So you're so shallow that my body disgusts you if it puts on a little extra weight?
Hey, Leela. I guess I got this for you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Oh. Thank you. You know what, Fry? I don't care if you're not the most important person in the universe. It really makes me happy to see you right now.
Hey!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Okay, so we haven't found any life yet. I still don't see why you men can't be happy with regular-sized miniature golf.
Fix it! Fix it! Fix it! Fix it! Fix it! Fix it! Fix it! Fix it! Fix it!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Only the Professor knows how to fix it. We have to wake him up.
Ah, come on. Bender loves mobs.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Only when he's in them and you know it. You really hurt his feelings.
At, uh, uh, a concert.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Ooh! Was it jazz noodling? My ex-boyfriend Sean played the sax. I used to listen for hours while he sat naked on my couch and improvised.
Dang! Can I get this wrapped up?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Ow! I might've liked Zapp Brannigan if he weren't a pompous dimwit who threw me in prison.
Whoa! Letters like "U" and "R" can mean words like "You" and "Are". Here, Leela, "U-R-2 Cute".

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Perhaps. What's your point?
Aha! My brother's grave!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Philip Fry, the original Martian.
I ordered a pizza.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Pizza delivery for... Icy Wiener. Yeah, very funny. Now cough up the $12.95.
Oh, yeah? Read it and weep. I'm a certified college dropout.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Please! Everyone knows 20th century colleges were basically expensive daycare centres.
The planet's kerploding!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Prepare for lift-off. We're out of fuel. Bender, I told you to fill the tank before we left.
Hey! When you look this good, you don't have to know anything.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Professor, We need to talk to you about Fry.
There's our man!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Professor, you'll offer Guenter the hat and, Fry, you'll offer him the banana. We'll let him choose whether he wants to be intelligent or just a mindless animal.
Ten minutes late. Ain't that just like a womanista?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Psst. Are you alone?

I know it may seem strange that I have feelings for an octopus monster from another universe. And yes, perhaps it's not the storybook romance that's been crammed down our throats by "Hollywood." But the Monsterpus has loved us from afar since we were amoebas. Only when the space anomaly opened could it finally express a billion years of longing.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Really? It loves us that much? Fire Diamondium cannon!
Well, I sort of a have a thing for this girl I work with.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Really? What type is she? You know, blonde, or Chinese, or Cyclops?
Leela, let's turn back. There's absolutely no shame in wussing out.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Relax. Everything'll be fine.
Hurry up! I wanna see the moon!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Relax. It's open till 9.
I can't. I have to go to the bathroom.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Robot's don't have bathrooms.
Hey, what's this goop?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Royal jelly. They feed it to the queen.
Hey, it's that "barbecue's over" sound again.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Sandstorm! We're in the eye of the storm!
I love these things!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Shake paws, Nibbler. Come on, shake. He might be a little hungry. Shake, boy. Usually he's had more ham by now. Shake!
Hermes has all the fun. Wait a second! He's got a Brain Slug on his head!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Shh! You're gonna get us all assimilated!
Mutants? That's the kind of thing you are.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Shh. You know mutants aren't allowed on the surface. If anyone asks, say I'm an alien, remember?
A gun?! D-Do I really need to—?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Shoot her! She's the robot!

Eating a sweet, innocent chick before it's even hatched?! Oh-ho-ho-ho, no, you won'tn't! I refuse to eat an unborn animal! I'm gonna keep this egg safe and warm and secure. Until it hatches out into the world. And then I'm gonna eat it!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Should we turn on the TV?
Hi, Leela! I'm just gonna keep talking, even if you can't hear me. Blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Shut up! I can hear you. The Professor says you're just a dream.
Yay!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Shut up, Fry. Now look, Adlai. I'm proud to be different. And I just wished I'd realised that when I was her age.
Oh, I had a nightmare I was in the year 2000 and you guys never existed. I'm so glad I'm awake now and you're really here.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Since when do you care about us?
Well, anyway, it's nice to have my own body back.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So how's the old corpse? Everything hooked up OK?
He's alive!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So that Moon hillbilly who got murdered was just an innocent husband and father!
Like my parents! Oh, wait, that was hitting.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So this language cartridge will let you distract them.
Didn't you see Frida Waterfall?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: So you did kill Frida Waterfall?
Why isn't this working?!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Some lazy or polite robot is holding it in.
This isn't Slurm at all!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Something's rotten on the planet Wormulon. Look at this.
You were mean and you yelled and you made us do all that work.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Sometimes a captain needs to do those things. Besides I, I thought we were friends.
I know you've rejected me a lot before but, frankly, I wasn't sure we were right for each other either. But now I am. So how 'bout a date tonight?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Sorry. I think I, um, I think I left my toaster on.
Leela! That's the second billboard you've crashed into this week!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Sorry. I was distracted by those protesters outside our building.
Incoming torpedoes. Shields at maximum yarnell!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Steady, Planet Express Ship. Focus on diverting all power to the scramjets.
I'm tellin' ya. Somethin' supernatural is happening. I'm scared to death!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Stop being ridiculous. There's no such thing as whatever you're saying.
I'm going down there to get my clover back. Some of the tunnels have metal bars so I'll need someone who's good at bending. Leela, how 'bout you?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Sure. I'll do it.
I guess that just leaves you and your fake fianc´... all alone... on a romantic cruise.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Take it off or I'll break it off.
Delivery boy? No! Not again! Please! Anything else!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Take your hands off me! You've been assigned the job you're best at just like everyone else.
Here, take my jacket. You look a little cold.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Thank you. It's all so beautiful. I forgot how many hundreds of degrees below zero it must be. I just wish I could convince the others you're alive.
Yes! Yes! That's exactly the job I've always wanted!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Thanks for the offer, Professor, but we don't have the proper career chips.
I hope you win, Leela.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Thanks, Fry. It's nice to have the support of viewers like you.
C'mon! Let's go tell Leela so we can grow up together!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Thanks, Professor. But I don't want the treatment.
Leela, we got lucky this time. But you should be more careful. I don't want anything to happen to you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Thanks, but I can look out for myself. Frankly, I can smell danger a mile away.
Yeah, I was going to thumb through that later.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That is completely reckless. Don't you ever think ahead?
That's marriage alright!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That is so unbelievably manipulative.

I know, and I've grown to accept that. Now I'm more interested in that new pizza parlour across the street. Kinda makes me pine for my days as a pizza delivery boy. "Here's you pizza," I'd say. "I didn't order any," they'd say. And then I'd be off to my next adventure.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That story stunk. Hand me the binoculars. I think the owner is from Cygnus 5.
Looks like this planet is next in line.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's Earth. The planet we live on.
No, not yet. How 'bout we go look for the original moon landing site?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's crazy! It's been lost for centuries!
How could you, Leela? I thought you had some standards. I mean, jeez, he's a dumb, gross gorilla!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's enough! Don't you think I feel bad enough already?
Who asked you to? I told you a hundred times to stop treating me like a baby. Now go. Go gather your nuts, you nagging grasshopper.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's it! I'm never helping you again! If anyone except you needs me, I'll be in the ship.
I don't see you anywhere.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's me over in Cootietown.
Then today's your lucky day, because I happen to be a holding, stroking, lovin' machine! Also spankin'.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's not even close to what I had in mind.
Nope. Not vaccinated either! Besides, it's not like one vote ever made a difference.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's not true; the first robot president won by exactly one vote.
Look, Leela, I'm sorry. I never should have dragged you out here.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's right, you shouldn't have. I still don't get what the big attraction is.
Ah, the scent of a rose. Curious how an aromatic chain of hydrocarbons can evoke our deepest emotions. For you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's such a beautiful thought, Fry. And what's more amazing, you expressed it without spewing crumbs at me.
I already did! So, Leela, do you wanna be like us? Or do you wanna be like Adlai with no severe mental or social problems whatsoever?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's the dumbest question I ever heard!
That's the secret ingredient of Slurm?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's the only ingredient of Slurm.
You know the worst thing about being a slave? They make you work but they don't pay you or let you go.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: That's the only thing about being a slave!
What do we care? We live in the United States.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: The United States is part of the world.
Man, that's dog's gonna be hard to beat. Look at him bring in the sheep! One sheep, two sheep... three sheep.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: The dog's good, but our real competition is the Hypno-Toad. Your turn, Nibbler, honey. Herd those sheep!
Oh, no! The gorilla! That's a par-four!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: The mouth's too dangerous. I'm going for the nose.
You'd better believe it!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: The old comedians were right, this place is a lot different from L.A.
Oh, no! The ice is melting!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: The pollution from the factory! It caused a greenhouse effect.
What's happening? Space cow?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: The ship's just taking the break-up a little hard. She's nuts!
No.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Then it wasn't space bandidos. Bender, lock down the ship. Don't let Flexo escape.
I can't tell you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Then why should I trust you? Why?
What if I refuse?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Then you'll be fired--
Trust me, I want twits that tittle.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Then you're gonna have to sink to Bender's level. Stop acting like the Queen of England.
Yo, that's messed up.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: There won't be any imploding once they read our environmental review. Right, Professor?
Leela, I'm no doctor, but I'm afraid you be exhibiting symptoms of illin'. You're risking all our lives for your own personal obsession.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: There's nothing personal about this! That thing screwed up my delivery! This time, it's business!

Bigfoot? Is that you? I'm not like the others, Bigfoot; I see through your monster coatings to the gentle loner inside. I bet you have a wounded racoon friend that you tenderly nurse back to health while you go... But in the end they shoot you. But you teach us about things. Oh. Just a flying saucer. Excuse me? You can't park here. The parking area's over there. Wow! Nice tube. Hey! Hey, what's the big idea? Stop abducting me. Why does your vanity plate say "Probe 1"?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: There's nothing so refreshing as the clean, crisp taste of this bold Canadian beer.
Yeah. If you rule out every guy with a lizard tongue or a low I.Q. or an explosive violent temper, of course you're gonna be lonely.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: There's nothing wrong with having high standards. Now can we please stop--
Oh, my God! The old Planet Express ship.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: There's the black box.
Wait, Mount Rushmore and the Leaning Tower of Pisa? I didn't know they were both in New York!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: They are now. In the 2600's, New Yorkers elected a super-villain governor, and he stole most of the world's monuments.
Why would Nixon stay at the Watergate?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: They give you a discount if you've been here before.
Stop! Thanks, Bender! Don't do it, Leela!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: They killed my parents!
Come on, Leela! Step your big boot down on the gas pedal.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: They've blown out one of our engines!
I'm no good at being a slave. I'm thinking about graduate school. Y'know, to become a barber?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This can't go on. Today is the day we fight back!
Hey! How come when I wanna do fun stuff that'll kill me you're against it?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This is more important than that marble-eating contest, Fry! It's about pride. Let me tell you a story from my childhood.
Let's dump it up!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This is the exact location of the dump. But there's nothing here.
I just let you back in!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This is unbelievable. I thought you were a furry little moron. But here you are flying an adorable spaceship. If only you could talk. Wait! I understood that! You say you're transmitting your thoughts directly to my brain. You say those awful flying brains are making everyone on Earth stupid? Oh, stupider. And you go on to say that we're headed for your home planet where your race has lived since the beginning of the universe? So, how did the universe begin? Then the meaning of existence-- So every religion is wrong!
Bender! It's a miracle! Ow!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This is, by a wide margin, the least likely thing that has ever happened.
Whoa, whoa! Slow down. You're going a mile a minute.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: This! You for this!
So, Leela, how about a romantic ride in one of those swan boats? They're kinda dangerous but I finally mastered them.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Those aren't swan boats, they're swans.
Hey! You have no right to criticise the 20th century. We gave the world the lightbulb, the steamboat and the cotton gin.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Those things are all from the 19th century.
The future is disgusting.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Typical 20th century attitude.
Ugh!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Ugh! Great. We're two days from Earth with no food.
What about what?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Uh... what if we go for a walk, possibly, because it's such a lovely day, perhaps.
Co-ed steam rooms! I love the future!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Uh, Fry, you're in the women's steam room.
Wow! Way to tell that guy off. Now what's your secret escape plan?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Uh, I guess to sit here and wait for death.
Whose that? The Queen of England?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Uh, e-e-excuse me. I have to...someplace.
Mind if we sit with you?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Uh, hey, why the hell would I? We're all guys here. Sweaty, hairy, gassy guys.
You remember when we first met?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Uh-huh. lt was right there in the cryogenic lab, eight years ago today.
OK, Leela, you'll be starring as Jenny--

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Uh-uh, forget it. A, I'm camera shy; and B, I get tongue tied in front of an audience armed with death rays.
Apology accepted. After all, you're only human.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wait a minute! You did it all backwards. Fry's the one who should be-- Oh, never mind!

My fellow fish monsters, far be it for me to question your stupid civilisation or its dumb customs, but is squeezing each other's brains out with a giant nutcracker really going to solve anything? Dr. Zoidberg is my friend, and though a woman has come between us, I say we'll always remain friends. And you know why? One reason. You bastard! I'll kill you! You bastard!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wait! Stop! Everyone is gone.
You were right. I don't know what it's like to be a mutant. But I want to know.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wait, I never meant for you to... Oh, no! Fry! Fry! No! No!
OK.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wait, hold on. It is actually possible to meet any celebrity you want.
Banana, banana, banana!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wait, what's that sound?
I want you to wake up.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wake up? But I'm not--
You have to wake up.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wake up? Oh, no! No! It can't be!
Wait. I thought we were buying our eyePhones online.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We are on line.
Can't we just cuddle? Nooo!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We can't wait for Bender. It's time for a woman's touch. Yah! Hi-yah! Yah, yah, yah!
Damnit, we'll have to fix the engine ourself.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We can't, you bastard! No one knows how it works. It's impossible!
Alright, scumwads. This one's for Bender's cocktail!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We did it! We won!
I am fully operational Captain.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We have to walk like robots, talk like robots and if necessary solve complex differential equations like robots.
But-But how do I know who's the human and who's the robot?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We just told you!
Hey, gimmie a break! What do you do with it?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We recycle everything. Robots are made from old beer cans.
Earth is dangerous. I fell off my chair there once. Ow! Quit it, Earth.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We won't even have to leave New New York! The package is going to Long Long Island.
It got us a lot of customers!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We're a delivery company!
What's this? This is the same toy surprise I got last time! I can't work under these conditions. And without me there is no mission. I am the mission!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We're back from the mission!
Nooo! I could fit if I didn't have these damn arms!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We're close to the exit. I can smell those filthy orange guys.
Are we at the fair yet, Mommy?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We're not at the any place! And we're out of fuel!
Stop! You're just goin' around in circles! Think, Fry, think! Everyone's depending on you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: We're too heavy. You guys need to lose some weight, fast!
Leela, I had worms. I needed to know who you loved. Me or them.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well... which of you wrote me that sonnet?
Silent? You've been meddling for two solid weeks.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well I can't just do that anymore. Your best friend is out there somewhere destroying himself.
But I don't like being a delivery boy.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well that's tough! Lots of people don't like their jobs but we do them anyway. You gotta do what you gotta do. Now hold out your hand. I'm gonna implant your career chip. It'll permanently label you as a delivery boy.
Oh. Then I must've fallen asleep.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well you were sure right about Flexo being evil.
I'm sorry you had to give up being a kid, Leela.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, I guess every adult wants to be a kid again sometimes. But I worked hard to be the person I am.
There but for the flip of a coin go we. So, um, Leela? Seeing how the universe wasn't destroyed, you wanna catch an ape fight? You know, together?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, I guess you deserve one more flip.
Aww. That's terrible, Leela. But imagine the look on their faces when you show up with two friends who eat all the hors d'Oeuvres.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, I wouldn't mind rubbing my success in a few choice faces.

Y'know, I guess it should be but, actually, I'm glad. I had nothing to live for in my old life. I was broke, I had a humiliating job and I was beginning to suspect my girlfriend might be cheating on me.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, at least here you'll be treated with dignity. Now strip naked and get on the probulator.
I don't get it. How can you say Lars is more mature than me?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, for one thing, his chequebook doesn't have the Hulk on it.
It'll be a rich, full day.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, goodnight. I'm gonna go make my dinners for the next month and freeze them.
I'm never going to get used to the 31st century. Caffinated bacon? Baconated grapefruit? Admiral Crunch?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, if you don't like that, try some Archduke Chocula.
What?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, let's divide up the china. I guess I'll take the NFC helmets and you can have the AFC helmets.
So, Leela, were you able to help the penguins?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, sure. I mean... not really. I mean... nature will work itself out. It can't screw things up any worse than we did trying to fix things, right?

Cause it-it taught me so much. Like how you should accept people, whether they be black, white, Klingon or even female. But most importantly, when I didn't have any friends, it made me feel like maybe I did.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, that is touchingly pathetic. I guess I can't let you go alone.
I'm telling you, Leela was cool, she was in command, and when she kicked people it hurt. It really hurt.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, this is the big moment. It's finally time to take my eye patch off.
Oh, yeah? Could a dream take you dancing in a Venusian garden?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, yes, technically. But it's still very sweet of you.
It worked perfectly!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Well, you downloaded Lucy Liu. Are you just going to stare vacantly at her and not say anything?
Like what?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Whale oil. Bender, lift it up to the can opener.
Now, when I say stupid things, guys all laugh and buy me stuff.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What a skank. Anyway, Planet Express is still facing foreclosure. There's no way we can raise enough money to save this company.
No.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What about that bathroom egg salad from the truck stop?
Well, it took an hour to write. I thought it would take an hour to read.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What are we supposed to do now?
I don't know what to do, Leela. Should I move in with Colleen and her four other boyfriends?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What are you going to do? Sleep in a big pile like hamsters?
Wait a second! Maybe your futuristic Xmas isn't so rotten after all.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What are you talking about, you crouton? You said it yourself Xmas should be about bringing people together, not blowing them apart.
All Leela ever wanted to do was help me. But I was to proud, too stupid to accept it. I wish I had died instead of her.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What are you talking about?
I'd like a sewer burger but without the rat faeces.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What are you, on a diet?
Cool. What's for dinner?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What do you mean "a scam"?
I had the Professor analyse the Alienese letter that was found with you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What does it say?
Leela, there's something I've wanted to tell you for a long time but every time I try I get nervous and my mouth feels like it's stuffed with peanut butter, even when it's not.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What is it? Is it about Bender?
Finally, the atom is safe.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What is it? My God! Did you hear maracas?
Leela, wait. You're making a mistake. You have no idea what's really going on.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What is really going on?
And me.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What was that? Oh, my God! We're heading straight into a black hole.
I don't know. I got nervous and I started thinking about neck bolts. Wow! Did you see that vase break? It was all like--

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What's happened to you?
Please, it's important to me.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What's that supposed to mean?
Yeah, yeah, I've gotten used cars before.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What's that? One of those Jefferson Starships I've heard so much about?
Not beautiful enough! A swell gal like you deserves better!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What's that?! Is my eye playing trick on me?! It's so beautiful! Fry, you've created a new colour! Totally different from any other colour or combination of colours.
I'm not going out with Amy. It's just to fool her parents. Hey, you're not jealous, are you?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What? No. No! Of course not!
Uh, not everything.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What? What do you mean?
Nothing. I got rid of the worms.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: What? Why would you do that?
But your parents are gross sewer mutants.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: When I was an orphan, I always wished I could grow up with my mom and dad. And now, thanks to being hurled backwards in time--
Ooh, nice cake. Sorry, I'm late.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Where have you—? Nah, it's fine.
Alright, team, let's go find that clover!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Which way to your house? The sign says we're at 71st Street.
Unbelievable. It's an actual, factual Robot Hell.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Who would've thought hell would really exist? And that it would be in New Jersey!
Shucks. It's still only half as beautiful as you. Whoa!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Whoa! I wish this moment could last forever.
Ow! Ow! Ow!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Whoa. Maybe you're right. I only meant to slap you twice.
Wait. Let me. Bender and I have our disagreements, but we're still friends and I'm gonna show him what that means. To the ship.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Why don't you just walk? He was only about 20 yards from here.
Married? Jenny can't get married.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Why not? It's clever, it's unexpected.
Under the seat.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Why won't it start?
Nooo! That's it I'm gettin' the hell outta here. Ooh! Ow!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Why, if it isn't my favourite head on Amy's body Fry.
The fabulous person!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: With friends like you guys--
OK, crow, prepare to be scared. And then, "honk, honk," the car honked its own horn!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wow! A talking scarecrow. Wanna come with us to see the Professor? He might be able to give you a brain.
Yeah, what did they ever do for me?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wow! The most humdrum activities look almost exciting through your eyes. What should we do next?
Yee-haw!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wow, look at that Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the solar system.
Nope!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wow. Superpowers! I'll be able to pack my day with twice as many humdrum activities.
Please, let me make it up to you. I'll treat you to a fancy birthday dinner tonight at Cavern on the Green.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Wow. That'll be the nicest place I've ever been stood up.
So, heads or tails?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Y'know, let's just say it's heads.
Hey, wait a minute! Isn't anyone gonna defend us?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yeah! I mean, he might not have a case, but I'm genuinely not human.
Are you okay, Leela?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'm just a little down 'cause the only man I'll ever love left me at the altar. Plus I live in a dumpster.
Look. I've been studying how to pilot the ship. Impressed?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yeah, actually. You're doing OK. The core reactor temperature's nominal, the blinker's off.
Man, we look stupid. We should've gotten store bought costumes.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yeah, but there wasn't a Woolworth's in this quadrant.
We're saved!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yeah, but this garbage ball's unstoppable now. New New York is done for.
Hey! You burned my cheek!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yeah, sorry, I wasn't really concentrating.
I would, but I ate a bunch of potato salad, so...

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's what I thought. You are all surface.
Wh-What if we helped you get your passion back without the hassle of mutilating me?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yeah, we know a great place in the mountains. We could take you there for a romantic dinner under the stars.
Look out! We're heading straight for those trees!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yeah, yeah, relax. Trees down.
Wait a minute! Is that blimp accurate?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yep. It's December 31st, 2999.
Check.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yes, sir! Ability to command the loyalty of sea creatures?
We missed the turn. We'll never catch them.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yes, we will. This sewer goes right under Planet Express, and it's 9pm!
Leela, is the person that parrot is mimicking telling the truth by proxy?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Yes. My parents were so hurt, I couldn't help it! But I distinctly told them not to tell anyone.
Look out! You want her, you're gonna have to go through me!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You call that a wound? That's a boo-boo tops. But thanks for trying to save me, Fry. Fry?! He's... he's dead!
I've been sitting right here. I picked up my life exactly where I left off a thousand years ago. Now, if you'll excuse me, it's eight o'clock. Time to get biz-ay!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You can't just sit here in the dark listening to classical music.
Wait, I'll be back in a minute.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You did it, Fry!
Leela! Bender! I missed you so much!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You did? What happened?
Wait, I know her.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You do not, you big fat liar. You don't know anyone. All you do is watch TV.
I am so, so sorry for what I did. And I know I can never make it up to you.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You don't have to apologize. In fact, I came to thank you.
I'm about to. Leela, let me play for you one for time.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You don't have to do that. I'm still seduced from before.
No, Leela. Brain make people smart.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You go fight biggest brain of all.
Guess I better head over to my night job.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You have a night job?
Eh?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You haven't been to work in three days. What have you been doing?
Um, I have a question. What if Bender was really giant?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You idiot! We already saw that.
Bender, I really hope that's you. 'Cause if it isn't... we're in trouble!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You jerk. Why'd you have to drag us along?
Valentine's Day's coming? Oh, crap! I forgot to get a girlfriend again. Well, since neither of us has a date, why don't we???

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You just assume I can't get a Valentine's date?
I can't tell you, Leela. You just have to trust me.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You keep saying that, but you have to give me something to go on or I...
Bender's gonna be killed!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You know what else I could use? A weekend at one of those fancy spas. And a Toblerone.
Not at all. It's just another thing that makes you a very special lady.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You mean, like my penis? Eh!
What I'm tryin' to say is... In all the world, I couldn't find a diamond good enough for you. But then I found one out there... Among the stars. The beautiful, affordable stars.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You mean... When you disappeared up on the comet...
Here I come. Let me just-- One more taste.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You pig. Stop stuffing your craw and save us.
We are cleared for takeoff.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You put Goofus and Ganja in charge? I'm the only trained pilot here.
Psht, I'm not crazy.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You sure you're okay, Fry? You do have tin foil on your head.
That clover helped my ratfink brother steal my dream of going into space. Now I'll never get there.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You went there this morning for doughnuts.
What? That's not fair. I deserve the same respect any other college dropout gets. By God, I'm gonna enroll here at Mars University and drop out all over again!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You won't last two weeks.
Everything was going great. Then, all of a sudden, she's talking about hanging out. Hanging out? She's getting way too serious. I'm not a one woman man, Leela.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You'll be back to zero soon enough.
Oh, no! My ATM card! My secret PIN number -- 1077. I've got nothing left. Except...

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You're Fry's relative. Do you have any idea how he got so crazy?
Well, at least my assassin will get what's coming to him.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You're in tremendous danger, you idiot! Half of these Emperors were drunk at their own coronation.
Stand back. I'm a tool-bot.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You're not a tool-bot. You're not a food-motron. You're not a robot of any kind.
A tomato.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You're not gonna eat a sandwich from a truck stop men's room are you?
But you're better than normal, you're abnormal. If you ask me, you shouldn't care what other people think.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You're right! I'll start by not caring what you think! I'm getting the surgery.
Hey, it's your fault. He only flushed himself because your emotions made him feel bad.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You're right. I feel terrible.
This is an emergency. Amy made Valentine's plans with some goon and I'm gonna be stuck there, lonely and miserable. Will you be my date, please?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You're too late, Fry. I'm sharing Valentine's Day with a very special man. He's not Zapp Brannigan or anything!
Affirmative. I feel nothing. I am a robot. Beep, beep, beep...

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You've made a terrible mistake. He's a human being, not a machine. Oh, Fry!
Things like me or... Things like this badminton racket?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: You, Fry. Bender, while you still have your giant brain, please... Tell me If Fry an' I ended up together—
Cause you're too ugly to be a wart.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Your Medicare dollars at work.
Hey, Leela, look at me!

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Your face can take a lot of punishment. That's good to know.
Y'know, I'm the luckiest guy in the whole future. I've been given a second chance and this time I'm not going to be a total loser. What's that?

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Your permanent career assignment.
Nope. Must be some weird alien emotion.

dialogue.speaker: Leela
dialogue.text: Zoidberg said some dumb stuff but he's a nice guy, really. It's just that Fry's been telling him what to say and Fry's a... do you have idiots on your planet?
